entries.text: 155 - قال: وكتب إلى إبراهيم بن سويد يقول: حدثني زيد بن أسلم في هذه الآية: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله}، قال: النداء حين يخرج الإمام، وكان يقول: السعي العمل، إن الله يقول: {إن سعيكم لشتى}، وقال: {من أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها}.
entries.text_ar: 155 - قال: وكتب إلى إبراهيم بن سويد يقول: حدثني زيد بن أسلم في هذه الآية: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله}، قال: النداء حين يخرج الإمام، وكان يقول: السعي العمل، إن الله يقول: {إن سعيكم لشتى}، وقال: {من أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها}.
entries.text_en: He said: Ibrāhīm b. Suwayd wrote to me, saying: Zayd b. Aslam narrated to me regarding this verse: ‘O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, hasten (fa-sʿaw) to the remembrance of God’ [62:9]: he said: ‘The call is [made] when the imām comes out.’ And he used to say: ‘Al-saʿy is [simply] action. God says: “Indeed, your efforts (saʿyakum) are diverse” [92:4]; and He said: “And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives (saʿā) for it with its [due] striving”’ [17:19].

entries.text: إلي منه، فقال له الصديق أبو بكر: والله إنه خير من ملء الأرض ذهبا. قال له أبو سفيان: اشتره مني! قال له أبو بكر: قد اشتريت هذا العبد الذي على ديني، بعبد مثله على دينك، فرضي أبو سفيان، فاشترى أبو بكر بلالا- رضي الله عنه فأعتقه. قال أبو سفيان لأبي بكر- رضي الله عنه: أفسدت مالك ومال أبي قحافة. قال: أرجو بذلك المغفرة من ربي. قال: متى هذا؟ قال أبو بكر- رضي الله عنه: يوم تدخل سقر تعذب. قال: أليس تعدني هذا بعد الموت؟ قال: نعم. قال: فضحك الكافر واستلقى. وقال: يا عتيق أتعدنى البعث بعد الموت؟ وتأمرني أن «أرفض «1» » مالي إلى ذلك اليوم؟ لقد خسرت واللات والعزى إن مالك قد ضاع، وإنك لا تصيب مثله أبدا. قال له أبو بكر- رضى الله عنه-[242 ب] : والله، لأذكرنك هذا اليوم يا أبا سفيان. فأنزل الله- عز وجل «فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطى وَاتَّقى» وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى - 6-

entries.text_en: than he. Al-Ṣiddīq Abū Bakr said to him: By God, he is better than the whole earth filled with gold. Abū Sufyān said to him: Buy him from me! Abū Bakr said to him: I have bought this slave, who is on my religion, for a slave like him who is on your religion. Abū Sufyān agreed; so Abū Bakr bought Bilāl (may God be pleased with him) and freed him. Abū Sufyān said to Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him): You have ruined your wealth and the wealth of Abū Quḥāfa. He said: By that I hope for forgiveness from my Lord. He said: When is this? Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said: The day you enter Saqar, to be tormented. He said: Do you not promise me this after death? He said: Yes. He said: The disbeliever laughed and fell on his back, and said: O ʿAtīq, do you promise me resurrection after death? And do you order me to «abandon» [1] my wealth until that day? By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, you have lost; your wealth is gone, and you will never get the like of it. Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said to him — [242b] — By God, I will remind you of this day, O Abū Sufyān. So God (Mighty and Majestic) revealed: «As for he who gives and fears God» «and believes in the best [reward]» (6)

surahMaterial.text_en: [Sūrat al-Layl (92): verses 1 to 21] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the night when it covers (1) and the day when it appears (2) and He who created the male and female (3) Indeed, your efforts are diverse (4) As for he who gives and fears God (5) and believes in the best [reward] (6) We will ease him toward ease (7) But as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need (8) and denies the best [reward] (9) We will ease him toward difficulty (10) And his wealth will not avail him when he falls (11) Indeed, upon Us is guidance (12) and indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life] (13) So I have warned you of a Fire blazing (14) None will burn in it except the most wretched (15) who denied and turned away (16) And the righteous one will be kept away from it (17) who gives his wealth to purify himself (18) and not for anyone with him is any favour to be rewarded (19) but only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High (20) And he is going to be satisfied (21)

surahMaterial.text_en: — this verse was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God have mercy on him). That is because he passed by Abū Sufyān — he is Ṣakhr ibn Ḥarb — and behold, he was tormenting Bilāl for his Islam, having placed a stone upon his chest and tormenting him with severe torment. Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God have mercy on him) said to him: Do you torment a servant for knowing his Lord? Abū Sufyān said: By God, no one has corrupted this black slave except you, you and your companion — meaning the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said to him: Would you sell him to me? He said: Yes. Abū Bakr said: By God, I do not find a price worthy of this slave. And also — [that] [4] is because Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him and make him pleased) passed by Bilāl the muezzin while his master Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī was tormenting him for Islam and saying: I will not leave you until you abandon the religion of Muḥammad; and Bilāl would say: One, One! Abū Bakr (may God have mercy on him) said: Do you torment a servant of God for believing in God (Mighty and Majestic)? His master Umayya said: Only you and your companion — meaning the Prophet ﷺ — have corrupted him for me; so buy him from me. He said: Yes. His master Umayya said: With what? Abū Bakr said: With a slave like him, on your religion. He agreed. So Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) went and bought a slave, took Bilāl (may God have mercy on them both) and freed him. Umayya said to Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him): If you had insisted on buying him for an ounce of gold, I would have given [him] to you «for it» [5]. surahMaterial.text_en: — this servant, meaning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him).
